Govind vs State Of Rajasthan (2023/Rjjd/016392) on 19 May,
2023

Author: Manoj Kumar Garg Bench: Manoj Kumar Garg [2023/RJJD/016392]
 HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR  S.B. Criminal Miscellaneous 2nd Bail Application No. 4691/2023 Govind S/o Sh. Kalu Ji Banjara, Aged About 27 Years, B/c Banjara, R/o Laanghnaj Vadsabha Road Jogni Mata Temple P.s.
Laanghnaj Dist. Mahesana (Guj.).

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
(Presently Lodged In Central Jail, Udaipur (Raj.))
 ----Petitioner  Versus State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp  ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Firoz Khan For Respondent(s) : Mr. SK Mehar, PP  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MANOJ KUMAR GARG Order 19/05/2023

The petitioner has been arrested in connection with FIR No.101/2022 of Police Station Salumber, District Udaipur, for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(3),
376(2)(N) of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act.

He has preferred this second bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C.
The first bail application was dismissed on merit by this Court vide order dated 02.12.2022.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that after rejection of the first bail application, some more prosecution witnesses have been examined before the court.
Counsel submits that the identity of the petitioner is highly doubtful in this case.
The victim in her statement has specifically named the accused as Ranjeet whereas the name of the petitioner is Govind.

The petitioner was implicated in this case merely on the basis of a [2023/RJJD/016392] (2 of 2) [CRLMB-4691/2023] notice under Section 133 of MV Act in which it was mentioned that the petitioner's actual name is Govind @ Ranjeet.
Counsel further submits that now the statement of the Investigating Officer has also been recorded but the said document i.e. notice has not at all been exhibited by the I.O.
This shows that the identity of the petitioner is not clear whether he is Govind or Ranjeet.
In such circumstances, benefit of bail should be granted to the accused- petitioner.

1
Learned Public Prosecutor has opposed the second bail application.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.
In her court statement, the victim has made specific averment that the petitioner had committed rape with her.
The victim was merely 15 years of age at the time of incident.
Till date, total 17 prosecution witnesses have been examined and now the trial is at the fag-end.
In such circumstances, without expressing any opinion on the merits and demerits of the case, I am not inclined to grant benefit of bail to the petitioner under Section 439 Cr.P.C.
Hence, the second bail application is rejected.
However, the trial court is directed to expedite the trial.

(MANOJ KUMAR GARG),J 96-MS/-
